title: WW2 - OverSimplified (Part 1)
beats: Skillshare sponsor read framed as Churchill could have used it
Mussolini's flip-flopping biography told as a rapid cartoon, ending with the haircut gag
Template for each dictator: humiliated nation, bad economy, weak government, strongman says he can fix everything
Versailles terms listed, then an invented 'spanking' rule, admitted as made up so you feel the humiliation
Japan introduced via 'let's rewind': isolation, unequal treaties, no resources, the West blocking its gains
'Here's the situation': three powers share racial superiority, hostility to Allies, want to expand
Hitler pushes the treaty, the Allies do nothing, twice, then appeasement acted as 'I want that thing' dialogue
Munich: Allies and Hitler dialogue; Chamberlain 'peace' paper then reversal
Italy takes Ethiopia/Albania, Japan stages incidents and invades China, Pact of Steel as 'relationship status'
Hitler-Stalin pact shown as dialogue with the betrayal hinted
Poland invaded, war declared, Phony War
France and UK list of outdated, passive habits showing they planned for the last war
Norway iron ore chain: request, refusal, mining, German pre-emption
Churchill replaces Chamberlain; Blitzkrieg through the Ardennes the Allies assumed was impenetrable, Dunkirk, fall of France
Hitler's mind games on the lone UK, puppet France, naval strike
Battle of Britain: Berlin raid provokes shift to London, RAF recovers; Part 1 stops on invasion postponed

new_moves.name: parallel-template-reuse
new_moves.what: Reuses a sentence skeleton so the viewer sees causes repeat across countries
new_moves.evidence: 2:48 and 3:36 near-identical wording for Italy and Germany

new_moves.name: rewind-insert
new_moves.what: Pauses the timeline to give a newcomer its backstory right when needed

theory: OverSimplified teaches causation by turning each country into a character with a consistent want, then reusing one grievance template so the viewer predicts the next dictator. Dialogue replaces exposition, so motive is shown as speech. The big weakness is that it never ramps difficulty or checks understanding.
velocity: Scene builder: give each concept a character with one stable motive so the learner can predict its next move
Voice: invented exaggerations are fine if flagged immediately as invented
Orchestrator: reuse an identical sentence skeleton across parallel cases to expose the pattern
Evals: ask the learner to predict the next country before showing it
Learner model: a rewind-insert beat should fire when a prerequisite is detected missing
